assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery that twisting bilayer graphene to a flat-band magic angle produces correlated insulators and superconductivity opened a new platform for strongly correlated matter. The theory predicted the flat bands and the experiment found clear signatures in nature, which is the pairing of idea and observation I value.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental discovery. This forms a clean theory-plus-experiment configuration. Others (e.g. Cao, Fatemi, Dean, Young, Yazdani) contributed and may be argued, but the supplied credit supports a fair three-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many groups across several moire systems in under a decade; the field is very active and the core observations are stable, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Microscopic mechanism of the superconductivity remains debated.
Credit to first-author experimentalists and to other moire platforms could complicate allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators established a new classification of quantum matter with robust edge and surface states, a conceptually deep and experimentally verified discovery with broad impact on condensed-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state; Molenkamp's group observed it experimentally in HgTe; Hasan demonstrated the three-dimensional topological insulator. Mele, Zhang, Bernevig and Hughes are also important and leaving them out is a real fairness issue; I select the three I judge most decisive from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of independent confirmation and a large body of follow-up work; the interpretation is stable and the recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan and uncredited theorists is contested.
The 2016 prize on topological phase transitions and phases may be seen as partly overlapping.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold dark matter with hierarchical structure formation is the standard framework linking the primordial fluctuations to galaxies and clusters. It is a foundational insight tied to many observations, including the cosmic web and galaxy rotation and lensing evidence.
assessment.attribution: White and Rees formulated the core-condensation galaxy formation picture; Faber contributed observational and early CDM framework work. Others such as Frenk, Davis, Blumenthal and Primack are also central and are not in the supplied credit, so the configuration is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Strongly supported by large-scale structure, CMB and lensing data; the nature of dark matter itself is still unknown, but the structure-formation framework is mature.
uncertainties: Credit is diffuse across a large community.
The Nobel committee may consider the framework partly covered by the 2019 cosmology prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, based on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and realized to extraordinary precision, are a measurement revolution that tests fundamental physics and opens new possibilities for geodesy and searches for new physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori conceived the magic-wavelength lattice clock; Ye's group brought it to record accuracy and stability. A compact two-person configuration with clear contributions, although Hall and Hansch (2005, frequency combs) are earlier laureates in the related area.
assessment.maturity: Independently realized and compared around the world; redefinition of the second is under discussion, which marks maturity.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier recognition of frequency combs and ion clocks (Wineland).
Other lattice-clock groups may claim credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 completed the Standard Model and confirmed a prediction made half a century earlier. It is among the most important discoveries in particle physics.
assessment.attribution: The prize to Englert and Higgs in 2013 recognized the theory; experimental credit is spread across thousands of people. Four credited names cannot all be included; I choose Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee as proposers and spokespersons of the experiments, with Della Negra left out reluctantly. The Nobel statutes make an experimental-collaboration prize awkward.
assessment.maturity: The discovery is thoroughly confirmed by two experiments and by subsequent coupling measurements; timeliness is a matter of statutory fit rather than evidence.
uncertainties: Collaboration credit is inherently hard to allocate to three people.
Whether the committee considers the discovery already recognized in 2013.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller's proposals for quantum gates with trapped ions and for quantum simulation with cold atoms created concrete architectures for quantum computing and simulation, with experimental realizations following.
assessment.attribution: The two-person credit is clear and well documented; the 2012 prize to Wineland and Haroche covered experimental control of single quantum systems, so there is some overlap, and experimental groups (Blatt, Monroe, Wineland) carried out the gate demonstrations.
assessment.maturity: Realized experimentally in ion traps and neutral atom systems; the field is mature and still growing, with commercial development.
uncertainties: Primarily theoretical credit; the experimental demonstrations belong to others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy by observing a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and associating a neutrino with a blazar flare, and later the Galactic plane. This is a discovery in nature with fundamental importance.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the project, Karle and Spiering were central in construction and analysis. A cohesive configuration, but collaboration credit extends well beyond three people.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed by multiple analyses; source identification is still developing (NGC 1068, TXS 0506+056) so full maturity is arguable.
uncertainties: Source association evidence is still moderate in significance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* provide direct evidence of black-hole shadows, connecting strongly to my interest in horizons and strong-field gravity. The imaging is of high visibility and scientific value.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed shadow imaging, Doeleman led the VLBI development and the collaboration, and Narayan provided theoretical modeling of accretion flows. The collaboration is large, and other leaders (e.g. Broderick, Loeb, Bower) may be argued.
assessment.maturity: Two sources imaged and results consistent with general relativity, but tests of alternatives are limited by resolution; the black hole physics was already honored in 2017 and 2020.
uncertainties: Limited precision to discriminate against alternatives to Kerr.
